description: Schema finalization + rewrite the two wrong-auth service clients to the verified live contracts. Lands the two additive schema edits (Card.scrydexId, SyncLog composite index) and pushes the enriched schema to the dev DB, then rewrites pokewallet.service.ts (PRICING ONLY, api.pokewallet.io + X-API-Key) and scrydex.service.ts (dual X-Api-Key/X-Team-ID headers, resolveScrydexCard/fetchScrydexCardById, pickRawPrice/pickGradedPrice, identifyCard, DELETE fetchPriceHistory), exports ApiTcgProduct, and runs the one-time live Vision/One-Piece-slug probe. Foundational: everything downstream queries the schema and imports these clients.
steps: schema.prisma (design §0.1/§3.2a/§3.6): add nullable `scrydexId String? @unique` to model Card and `@@index([job, cardId, ranAt])` to model SyncLog. Both additive — no drops/narrowing. Then `npx prisma validate` and `npm run db:generate`.

DB push (design §0.1, MEDIUM-RISK shared system — call it out in findings when run): `npm run db:push` against the worktree .env DATABASE_URL. Additive/non-destructive (new tables current_price/sync_log, new columns, 2 enums, scrydexId, index). Rollback note in design §0.1.

card.service.ts line 498: add `export` to `interface ApiTcgProduct` so the sync's One Piece fetcher (FEAT-002) reuses the exact shape. No behaviour change. (apitcg `images` is an ARRAY — line 504 `const img = p.images?.[0]` — leave the existing One Piece catalog code as-is.)

REWRITE pokewallet.service.ts (design §2): POKEWALLET_BASE_URL=`https://api.pokewallet.io`; `pokeWalletHeaders()` returns `{ 'X-API-Key': process.env.POKEWALLET_API_KEY }` (throw if unset). Export `interface OnePiecePrice { market:number|null; low:number|null; currency:string }`. `fetchOnePieceSetPrices(setCode): Promise<Map<string,OnePiecePrice>>` via GET /op/sets/{setCode}?page=1&limit=200 keyed by card_number. `fetchPokemonCardPrice(name): Promise<OnePiecePrice|null>` via GET /search?q=<name>. Pure helper `pickOnePiecePrice(card)` reads tcgplayer.prices.market_price|low_price, falls to cardmarket.prices.avg|low, else null — NEVER throws on CM-only `tcgplayer:null`. `num()` returns finite >0 else null. Zod schemas per §2.2 (OpTcgPlayerSchema nullable, OpCardSchema, OpSetResponseSchema, PwSearchResponseSchema). Error paths return empty Map / null + single console.warn. DELETE fetchOnePieceSets/fetchOnePieceCards/the /prices/pokemon/{id} endpoint.

REWRITE scrydex.service.ts client (design §3.1–§3.4, keep Prisma-free): SCRYDEX_BASE_URL=`https://api.scrydex.com`; `scrydexHeaders()` sends BOTH `X-Api-Key` + `X-Team-ID` (throw if either env missing). `gameSlug(game:Game)` literal map POKEMON->'pokemon', ONE_PIECE->'onepiece'. Zod ScrydexCardSchema/VariantSchema/PriceEntrySchema/TrendDeltaSchema + ScrydexSearchResponseSchema + ScrydexSingleCardResponseSchema per §3.2 (always append ?include=prices). `resolveScrydexCard({name,number,setName?,setCode?,game})` searches GET /{slug}/v1/cards?q=name:<name>&pageSize=25&include=prices, matches on normNumber(entry.number??printed_number)===normNumber(card.number) AND set (prefer expansion.code===setCode when setCode known — One-Piece-only via externalId prefix — else case-insensitive expansion.name===setName), tie-break per §3.2a, returns `{scrydexId:matched.id, card:matched}` or null (NO 2nd call; carry a comment that setCode is optional/One-Piece-only and Pokemon matches on setName+number — NIT-3). `fetchScrydexCardById(scrydexId,game)` via GET /{slug}/v1/cards/{scrydexId}?include=prices. `pickRawPrice(card)` first `type==='raw'` entry with finite market/low -> {market,low,currency,trends,variant,condition} with variant verbatim from variant.name (default 'normal') and condition verbatim from entry.condition (default 'NM'); null when absent. `pickGradedPrice(card,grade,company?)` filters `type!=='raw'` && company.toUpperCase()===(company??'PSA') && normalizeGrade(grade)===normalizeGrade(requested) reusing graded-price parseGrade; null when absent. `identifyCard(imageBase64): Promise<ScrydexIdentifyResult|null>` where `ScrydexIdentifyResult { cardId; confidence; name; setCode }` and cardId carries the EXTERNAL catalog id (load-bearing comment per §3.1 so recognize/route.ts stays unchanged). DELETE fetchPriceHistory.

LIVE PROBE (design §3.5 / §4; the ONLY live network in this FEAT — space calls 3–5s apart per the Cloudflare note): throwaway `scripts/probe-scrydex-vision.ts` POSTs the contracts' not-yet-tried Vision candidates (/v1/vision, /pokemon/v1/vision/identify, /v1/image/match, /pokemon/v1/cards/vision) with a real small base64 image, and one GET /onepiece/v1/cards?q=name:luffy&pageSize=1&include=prices to confirm the One Piece slug. If a Vision path resolves -> wire identifyCard to it + Zod-parse body + load-bearing comment naming the resolved path. If none -> KEEP null->Tesseract fallback and write 'Vision UNRESOLVED as of <date>' in the service doc-comment (recorded in findings + checklist). If the One Piece slug 404s -> record 'Scrydex One Piece scoped out until slug confirmed; One Piece chart empty = expected'. Delete the probe script afterward. NEVER fabricate a match.

Record in FEAT findings: db:push outcome, the Vision probe result (resolved path or UNRESOLVED), the One Piece slug result, and any slug/endpoint caveat the downstream FEATs and the checklist must reflect.
acceptance_criteria: `npx prisma validate` passes and `npm run db:generate` produces a client with Card.scrydexId; `npm run db:push` applies current_price/sync_log/card.scrydexId/enriched pricing_history to the dev DB (AC per design §0.1).

pokewallet.service.ts calls api.pokewallet.io with X-API-Key; the .com/v1 domain, Authorization: Bearer, /prices/pokemon/{id}, /one-piece/sets, /one-piece/sets/{id}/cards, fetchOnePieceSets, and fetchOnePieceCards are all gone (AC-1).
scrydex.service.ts sends BOTH X-Api-Key and X-Team-ID on every request; building headers without SCRYDEX_TEAM_ID throws; fetchPriceHistory is deleted (AC-4).
interface ApiTcgProduct is exported from card.service.ts with no behaviour change.

The Vision endpoint is either wired (documented path) OR explicitly documented UNRESOLVED with the null->Tesseract fallback intact; the One Piece slug is confirmed or its contingency documented; no fabricated match path exists (AC-7).

`npm run type-check` passes for the rewritten clients (downstream sync call-site is updated in FEAT-002 — if type-check surfaces the sync's stale fetchPokemonCardPrice(c.id) usage, that is expected and fixed in FEAT-002; note it in findings).
verification: npm run db:push  (dev DB; MEDIUM-RISK — note in findings)
npm run type-check  (clients compile; the sync call-site mismatch, if any, is FEAT-002's)
findings:
SCHEMA: added nullable `Card.scrydexId String? @unique` + `SyncLog @@index([job, cardId, ranAt])`; both additive. `npx prisma validate` passed, `npm run db:generate` produced a client with Card.scrydexId.

DB:PUSH (MEDIUM-RISK, remote Supabase dev DB at aws-0-ap-northeast-1.pooler.supabase.com): ran via `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` (CLI prompts interactively otherwise). SUCCEEDED — 'Your database is now in sync with your Prisma schema' in 5.34s. The lone warning was the standard unique-constraint note for the new `scrydexId` column; it is a brand-new all-NULL column so there are zero duplicates — the push is non-destructive/additive (new current_price/sync_log tables, enriched pricing_history, 2 enums, scrydexId, index). Rollback per design §0.1 if ever needed.

VISION PROBE (one spaced live run, calls 4s apart; throwaway script created + deleted): ALL FOUR candidate paths returned HTTP 404 — /v1/vision, /pokemon/v1/vision/identify, /v1/image/match, /pokemon/v1/cards/vision. Vision is UNRESOLVED as of 2026-10-02. identifyCard() returns null and recognize/route.ts degrades to on-device Tesseract (the verified existing fallback). The service doc-comment records this. The CHECKLIST must state: card scanning uses Tesseract fallback (Scrydex Vision endpoint unconfirmed) — never fabricate a match.

ONE PIECE SLUG: CONFIRMED. GET /onepiece/v1/cards?q=name:luffy&pageSize=1&include=prices returned HTTP 200 with data (e.g. id 'OP17-030', number '30', printed_number 'OP17-030'). So the `onepiece` slug and the search+include=prices shape work for One Piece too — resolveScrydexCard covers One Piece and One Piece charts are NOT scoped out. NOTE for downstream: for One Piece the Scrydex native `id` can equal the Bandai code while `number` is the bare collector number ('30'); normNumber() handles the bare-vs-'/total' form, and set match prefers expansion.code===setCode (One-Piece-only via externalId prefix) else case-insensitive expansion.name===setName (Pokemon).

CLIENTS: pokewallet.service.ts rewritten (api.pokewallet.io + X-API-Key, PRICING ONLY: fetchOnePieceSetPrices + fetchPokemonCardPrice + pure pickOnePiecePrice; .com/v1, Bearer, /prices/pokemon/{id}, /one-piece/*, fetchOnePieceSets, fetchOnePieceCards all deleted). scrydex.service.ts rewritten Prisma-free (dual X-Api-Key+X-Team-ID headers that throw if either env missing, gameSlug, resolveScrydexCard, fetchScrydexCardById, pickRawPrice, pickGradedPrice reusing graded-price parseGrade [now exported], identifyCard->null; fetchPriceHistory deleted). card.service.ts: `export` added to interface ApiTcgProduct (no behaviour change). graded-price.ts: parseGrade exported for reuse.

TYPE-CHECK: the two rewritten clients + card.service.ts compile clean. The ONLY remaining type errors are in src/lib/services/sync-cards.service.ts (lines 439/464/468/480): stale `fetchOnePieceSets`/`fetchOnePieceCards` imports and `fetchPokemonCardPrice(c.id).marketPrice` usage against the new OnePiecePrice shape. These are EXPECTED and are FEAT-002's job to rewire (per FEAT-001 AC-6). LINT passes clean.
